title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: I do not recall the specific details of the starting material. As a guess, it might have been an NbMoTaW-based high-entropy alloy used as the initial material.
recollection.intervention: I do not recall the specific details. As a guess, the authors processed the alloy to induce chemical short-range order, perhaps through specialized heat treatments or alloying modifications.
recollection.structure: I do not recall the specific details. As a guess, the structure might be a partially ordered arrangement of the refractory elements in the high-entropy alloy matrix.
recollection.mechanism: I do not recall the specific details. As a guess, the short-range order could reduce phonon scattering by creating a more ordered local environment, thereby enhancing heat conduction.
recollection.results: I do not recall the specific details. As a guess, they might have found that the presence of short-range order increased the lattice thermal conductivity compared to a fully random solution.

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies inducing SRO and partial local ordering, and incorrectly guesses heat treatment/alloying rather than Monte Carlo-controlled SRO with HfTi/TiZr clusters and percolation. The proposed reduction in phonon scattering from a more ordered local environment aligns with the actual reduced-lattice-distortion mechanism, but omits percolation pathways and phonon-DOS changes. It gives no numerical result such as the ~12% increase, and the qualitative increase is already stated in the title.
